meta.label: Secondhand marketplaces
tradeoffLabels: seller keeps more of the sale price
buyer is protected if something goes wrong
meta.attribution: This compares general marketplaces and giving networks for secondhand goods across categories, not the clothing-specific resale apps already covered in the Clothing realm's own secondhand and resale lens. Fee and protection figures come from each platform's own published fee policy, help center article or terms of service, read directly, plus Etsy's 2025 annual report filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission for Etsy's seller fees. Where a platform states a US, UK, German or Spanish figure, other countries it operates in may set different terms; the Kleinanzeigen and Wallapop pages were read in German and Spanish. Some marketplaces charge more but do more of the work: AptDeco collects and delivers furniture itself, and Back Market sells refurbished electronics from professional sellers with a 12-month warranty, so private individuals cannot list there at all. These figures change without much notice, so check the linked page before relying on a number here. Facebook Marketplace, probably the most used option in this category in the United States, was left out of the first pass because its help center returned errors to automated requests; it was added in October 2026 once its fee and Purchase Protection pages could be read directly. Its protection, like Gumtree's, only covers purchases paid through its own checkout, and Craigslist has no payment system or protection at all. Three routes cost nothing at all and involve no marketplace fee at any point: Freecycle, the Buy Nothing Project and, in the UK, Freegle, all of which exist only to give things away locally. Two more, Habitat for Humanity ReStore and the Salvation Army's thrift stores, sell donated goods in person with no listing or shipping step, and put the proceeds into building homes or funding community programs rather than into a marketplace's own revenue. Reviewed 2026. Not an endorsement; check the linked source page on each option for its current terms.

criteria.label: Low seller fees, seller keeps more of the sale
Buyer protection if an item is fake, damaged or never arrives
Easy and immediate, without listing or shipping

products.name: eBay
products.description: General online marketplace selling secondhand and new goods across almost every category, by auction or fixed price, shipped by the seller after the item sells.

fees.note: eBay's own selling fees page says eBay charges two main types of selling fees: an insertion fee when a listing is created, and a final value fee when the item sells; the general final value fee for most categories is 13.6% of the total sale amount up to $7,500 per item, plus a small per-order fee.

buyer_protection.note: eBay's Money Back Guarantee page says coverage is automatic, covers the purchase price plus original shipping on eligible purchases, and that there is no extra fee for the coverage.

products.name: Mercari
products.description: Shipped, app-based marketplace for secondhand and new goods across most categories, with items listed, sold and shipped through the app.

fees.note: Mercari's own help center article on fees says a 10 percent selling fee applies to the item price plus any buyer-paid shipping, for listings created or updated on or after January 6, 2025.

buyer_protection.note: Mercari's own Buyer Protection article says buyers get a full refund for eligible returns when an item is not as described, that the protection applies a 3.6 percent fee, and that buyers have 72 hours after confirmed delivery to report an issue before payment is automatically released to the seller.

products.name: Vinted
products.description: Peer-to-peer marketplace, mostly secondhand clothing but expanding into other categories, where sellers set their own price and keep the full sale amount while buyers pay a separate protection fee.

fees.note: Vinted's own how-it-works page says: 'There are no selling fees on Vinted. You keep 100% of what you earn.'

buyer_protection.note: Vinted's own price list page says the Buyer Protection fee is a fixed $0.70 plus 5 percent of the item price, and its how-it-works page says buyers are covered when they shop and pay through Vinted.

products.name: Gumtree
products.description: UK classified ads site for local secondhand goods, with free basic listings and an optional in-app payment and buyer protection system.

fees.note: Gumtree's own help page on fees and selling costs says: 'There are no seller fees or costs when using payments on Gumtree.'

buyer_protection.note: The same Gumtree help page says the Buyer Protection fee charged to buyers at checkout is a flat 0.70 pounds plus a variable 5 to 10 percent of the item price, depending on its value and category.

products.name: Craigslist
products.description: Free local classifieds site organized by city, where buyers and sellers arrange their own pickup, payment and delivery with no built-in payment system.

fees.note: Craigslist's own fees FAQ says: 'Some types or categories of postings may have an associated fee.' Its US table lists For Sale by Owner postings at $0-5, with cars and trucks, motorcycles and RVs at $5, and states 'Publishing your posting is a one time charge. craigslist does not have any subscription fees, or additional charges.' There is no commission on the sale price, since Craigslist never handles the payment.

buyer_protection.note: Craigslist has no payment system and no buyer protection of any kind. Its terms of use say Craigslist provides the site 'AS IS' and 'any risk of using CL is assumed by you,' and disclaim 'any liability or responsibility for acts, omissions, or conduct of you or any party in connection with CL.' Its own avoiding-scams page offers one rule instead, 'Deal locally, face-to-face,' and warns buyers to beware of '"guaranteed" transactions or payment processing services' and that 'requests to use an escrow service can be a scam.' If an item turns out fake or broken after a cash handover, there is no platform to claim against.

products.name: Facebook Marketplace
products.description: Meta's classifieds section inside Facebook, used mostly for local pickup deals arranged in Messenger and paid in person, with an optional shipping and checkout system for sales across the continental US.

fees.note: Facebook's own help article on shipping says that for an item sold with shipping and checkout, 'A selling fee of 10% (or $0.80 minimum) will be deducted from the amount of the purchase,' the same rate as Mercari's. None of the Facebook help pages read for this entry lists any fee for a local pickup sale, which is paid between buyer and seller directly and never passes through Facebook.

buyer_protection.note: Facebook's Purchase Protection article says protection is free and automatic for eligible orders bought with shipping or checkout, and lets the buyer request a full refund of price and shipping if the order never arrived, arrived damaged or different than described, or the seller broke their own refund policy. The same article says 'Purchases made through third-party sites, local pickups, Messenger transactions, or through other messaging services don't qualify for Purchase Protection,' and the shipping article repeats 'Local pickup items aren't covered by Purchase Protection.' The score sits well below eBay's automatic guarantee because the local, in-person sale that most Marketplace listings are arranged as has no platform recourse at all.

products.name: OfferUp
products.description: Local and shipped marketplace app for secondhand and new goods, combining in-person meetups for local sales with an optional shipping and payment system for items sold further away.

fees.note: OfferUp's own Terms of Service say: 'You can post most items through the Services without charge. OfferUp charges a fee to post some items, for example, if you exceed your available free posts for certain types of items in certain categories.'

products.name: Nextdoor
products.description: Neighborhood social app with a For Sale & Free section for buying, selling and giving away items locally, alongside its main neighborhood feed.

accessibility.note: Nextdoor's own press release says neighbors use its buy, sell and give feature, including a Free Finds tool, to find items nearby, and that Nextdoor reaches 276,000 neighborhoods including nearly 1 in 3 US households, describing it as 'your trusted neighborhood treasure map.'

products.name: The Freecycle Network
products.description: Network of local giving groups where members post items they want to give away or are looking for, and arrange pickup directly with each other, for free.

fees.note: Freecycle's own about page says everything posted must be free, legal and appropriate for all ages, that membership is free, and that it is free to post messages.

accessibility.note: Freecycle's own about page says members post what they want to give or receive, other members reply, and 'you arrange a pickup time and location' directly with them, with no shipping step.

products.name: Buy Nothing Project
products.description: Hyperlocal gifting network organized into neighborhood groups, where members give away and ask for items with no money changing hands.

fees.note: The Buy Nothing Project's own homepage describes it as a 'global community for giving and getting stuff, completely for free.'

accessibility.note: The Buy Nothing Project's own homepage invites members to 'discover what your neighbors are giving away and find a new home for what you no longer need' within local groups.

products.name: Freegle
products.description: UK network of local groups for giving away unwanted items and finding things other people are giving away, for free.

fees.note: Freegle's own homepage describes it as 'like online dating for stuff... We'll match you with someone local. All completely free.'

products.name: Habitat for Humanity ReStore
products.description: Nonprofit home improvement and furniture stores that resell donated goods in person; proceeds fund Habitat for Humanity's home building and repair work.

accessibility.note: Habitat for Humanity's own ReStores page describes them as stores that accept donations and 'sell a constantly changing inventory of diverse, high-quality merchandise to the public at a fraction of the retail price,' a walk-in purchase with no listing or shipping step.

products.name: Salvation Army Thrift Stores
products.description: Nonprofit thrift store chain selling donated clothing and household goods in person; proceeds fund the Salvation Army's rehabilitation centers and community programs.

accessibility.note: The Salvation Army's own thrift stores page describes them as a way to buy gently used clothing, household items and other goods at 'significant savings over retail prices,' across 887 stores nationwide, with proceeds funding programs including 78 rehabilitation centers.

products.name: Etsy
products.description: Global online marketplace for handmade, vintage and craft goods, where independent sellers list items and ship them after a sale; vintage pieces are its main secondhand category.

fees.note: Etsy's 2025 annual report, filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission in February 2026, states that Etsy marketplace sellers pay a fixed listing fee of $0.20 for each item listed, a 6.5% transaction fee on each completed transaction including shipping, and Etsy Payments processing fees that typically vary between 3.0% and 6.5% of the total sale price plus a flat per-order fee. Sales that come through Etsy's Offsite Ads carry a further 12% or 15% fee. A typical US sale therefore costs the seller roughly 10% before any ad fee, a little less than eBay's 13.6% final value fee.

buyer_protection.note: Etsy's own help article on its Purchase Protection program says buyers get a full refund for qualifying orders when the item does not arrive, arrives damaged, arrives 7 or more days after the latest estimated delivery date, or differs significantly from its description or photos. The buyer first asks the seller for help, and if nothing is resolved after 48 hours can ask Etsy to step in. Change-of-mind returns depend on each seller's own policy. The help page refuses automated requests, so it was read through Etsy's public help center feed of the same article.

products.name: Back Market
products.description: Online marketplace for refurbished phones, laptops, consoles and other electronics, sold by professional refurbishers rather than private individuals, with a seller-backed warranty on every item.

buyer_protection.note: Back Market's own US warranty certificate requires every seller to give the buyer a 12-month limited warranty against defects from the delivery date, presumes any defect appearing in that period existed at delivery, and requires the seller to offer an exchange, repair or refund within five business days of getting the product back. It also states 'This Limited Warranty is not provided by Back Market, but by the Seller', with Back Market acting as intermediary. Back Market's US terms of service add a 30-day change-of-mind return, with the buyer paying return shipping. There is no seller-fee score here because private individuals do not list on Back Market; they can only sell through its trade-in offers.

products.name: Swappa
products.description: US peer-to-peer marketplace for used phones, laptops, tablets and other electronics, where staff check each listing before it goes live and payment runs through PayPal or Stripe.

fees.note: Swappa's own fees page says 'Listing is always free, but seller pays 3% of the sold price', that the buyer pays a separate 3% fee added to the listing price, and that PayPal (3.49% plus $0.49) or Stripe (2.9% plus $0.30) take their standard processing fees on top. A seller therefore keeps roughly 93% of the price before shipping.

buyer_protection.note: Swappa's own returns and refunds policy says 'If you did not receive what was advertised, you are entitled to a refund', that sellers must accept returns of items that are not as advertised or break its listing criteria, and that sellers are not required to accept change-of-mind returns. Refunds are paid by the seller, with Swappa staff mediating on the sale page and PayPal's own dispute process behind it. For a parcel that tracking shows as delivered but the buyer never got, the policy tells the buyer to go to local police. The score sits below Mercari's because Swappa itself does not refund the buyer.

products.name: AptDeco
products.description: US marketplace for used furniture and decor in which sellers list their own pieces and AptDeco's delivery team or partners collect the item, inspect it and deliver it to the buyer.

fees.note: AptDeco's own selling page says listing is free and that once an item sells the seller keeps up to 70% of the earnings, with AptDeco's share paying for advertising, pickup and delivery, listing photo editing and payment processing. Because AptDeco collects and delivers the item, the seller's cut is far lower than on a classifieds site, but the seller also does no shipping.

buyer_protection.note: AptDeco's own money-back guarantee page says a wrong item, a missing item or an item that does not match the listing is eligible for a full or partial refund, that the delivery team inspects each item at pickup, and that the buyer must open a dispute within 48 hours of delivery, after which payment is released to the seller. Sales are otherwise final; a buyer who simply does not like an as-described item can resell it on AptDeco with seller fees waived.

products.name: Chairish
products.description: US marketplace for vintage and secondhand furniture, art and decor, where private consignors and professional dealers list items that Chairish's team reviews before they go live.

fees.note: Chairish's own help article on selling plans says a private Consignor pays a 40% commission on everything sold on Chairish (20% on items sold through Chairish Auctions), while paid Professional, Premium, Plus, Elite and Platinum dealer plans pay between 20% and 30% on used and vintage items. An individual clearing out a home therefore keeps about 60%. The page refuses automated requests and was read through Chairish's public help center feed of the same article.

buyer_protection.note: Chairish's own Buyer Guarantee article says it covers an item that does not arrive, is materially different from its description or is broken in transit, and that its return policy separately gives 48 hours from delivery to request a return for any other reason, with Chairish holding the seller's payment until that window closes. Local pickup and seller-managed delivery orders are final once the buyer takes the item, and surface wear on vintage pieces is not covered.

products.name: Shpock
products.description: UK classifieds app for buying and selling secondhand goods locally, with an optional in-app payment, delivery and buyer protection service for items sent by post.

fees.note: Shpock's own terms and conditions say 'Shpock’s basic service is free of charge', and that paid extras are limited to visibility boosts and subscription memberships; its membership help page lists unlimited listings in standard categories as a member benefit, so heavy free users can hit a listing cap. The terms also say a seller paid through the PayPal option pays Shpock a commission and PayPal's own fee, without stating the commission rate. The Buyer Protection fee on posted sales is charged to the buyer, not the seller.

buyer_protection.note: Shpock's own Buyer Protection terms say the service is optional, available only with its integrated payment, and costs the buyer a fixed GBP 0.30 to 3.75 plus 0 to 15% of the item price. It refunds the full payment if an item is not delivered or significantly differs from its description or is damaged, but the buyer must report the problem within seven days of the seller sharing proof of postage and pays to send a faulty item back. Cash sales arranged in person have no cover. The score sits below Gumtree's similar optional scheme because the buyer carries the return cost even on a valid claim.

products.name: Preloved
products.description: UK classified ads site for secondhand goods, pets and vehicles, where buyers and sellers arrange payment and collection between themselves.

fees.note: Preloved's own membership page says a free account can place unlimited listings, but free members can only respond to other people's listings 12 days after they are created; a Full membership at £6 a year or Premium at £15 a year removes that wait. Business accounts pay £20 or £45 a month with 'No listing, selling or commission charges'. Preloved takes no share of any sale price.

buyer_protection.note: Preloved's own terms say Preloved is not a party to the contract between buyer and seller and that 'it is not our responsibility if a seller does not deliver Items, if the Items are not as described'. Its help page on paying for an item leaves the payment method to the two parties and suggests PayPal for distance purchases because PayPal will often compensate a buyer who does not get the item. Like Craigslist, there is no platform protection of any kind.

products.name: Kleinanzeigen
products.description: German classifieds site, formerly eBay Kleinanzeigen, for local secondhand sales with an optional escrow payment and buyer protection service called Sicher bezahlen for items sent by post within Germany.

fees.note: Kleinanzeigen's own help article on fees (in German) says using the site is free in principle for private sellers, who can post up to 100 ads in consumer goods, services and jobs within 30 days before a fee of 1.99 euros applies to each further ad. Cars, other vehicles and property have their own lower free limits and fees of 9.99 euros or more. Neither that article nor the article on selling with Sicher bezahlen lists any commission on the sale price; the Sicher bezahlen service fee is paid by the buyer.

buyer_protection.note: Kleinanzeigen's own help article on Sicher bezahlen (in German) says payment is held in trust by the licensed payment firm Adyen until the buyer confirms receipt, and that its buyer protection applies when an item is not sent, differs substantially from its description, is counterfeit, or is wrong or incomplete. It costs the buyer a service fee of 0.50 euros plus 4.5% of the price, covers only parcels sent within Germany, and the cost of returning a not-as-described item is not refunded. Cash deals arranged for collection are not covered.

products.name: Wallapop
products.description: Spanish secondhand marketplace app, also used in Italy and Portugal, for local in-person deals or for shipped sales paid through the app with Wallapop's buyer protection.

buyer_protection.note: Wallapop's own terms of use (in Spanish) say that on shipped sales the buyer can request a refund if they report within 48 hours of the carrier's delivery notice that the item is damaged or does not match the seller's description or photos, with Wallapop holding the payment until then. A refund covers the price, shipping and the protection fee, and a return handled through Wallapop's process is free for both sides. The same terms say the protection is not insurance. Its shipping page says the buyer pays the shipping and protection cost. In-person deals have no cover. No seller-fee score is given because none of the Wallapop pages read for this entry states whether private sellers pay a commission.
